request.query: For a nonzero integer multivariate polynomial there exist bounded order Hasse differential operators whose derivative determinant factors as a product in disjoint variables with degree bounds

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative of Order k on Polynomial Ring
items.type: {R : Type u_1} → [inst : Semiring R] → ℕ → Polynomial R →ₗ[R] Polynomial R
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ R $, the Hasse derivative of order $ k $ is an $ R $-linear map $ D^{(k)} : R[X] 	o R[X] $ defined by $ D^{(k)}(a_i X^i) =  inom{i}{k} a_i X^{i - k} $ on monomials and extended linearly. This operation generalizes the usual derivative by scaling each coefficient $ a_i $ by the binomial coefficient $  inom{i}{k} $ and reducing the degree by $ k $.

items.informal_name: Product Rule for Hasse Derivatives in Polynomial Rings
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k : ℕ) (f g : Polynomial R),
  (Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) (f * g) =
    ∑ ij ∈ Finset.antidiagonal k, (Polynomial.hasseDeriv ij.1) f * (Polynomial.hasseDeriv ij.2) g
items.informal_description: For any polynomials $ f, g \in R[X] $, the $ k $-th Hasse derivative of the product $ f \cdot g $ satisfies $$ D^{(k)}(f \cdot g) = \sum_{\substack{i + j = k}} D^{(i)}(f) \cdot D^{(j)}(g), $$ where the sum is taken over all pairs $ (i, j) $ of natural numbers such that $ i + j = k $. This expresses the Hasse derivative of a product as a sum over the antidiagonal decomposition of $ k $.

items.informal_name: Partial Derivative of Tensor Product Variable under Universal Factorization Map
items.type:
∀ (R : Type u_1) [inst : CommRing R] (n m k : ℕ) (hn : n = m + k) (i : Fin k) (j : Fin n),
  (MvPolynomial.pderiv (Sum.inr i))
      ((MvPolynomial.tensorEquivSum R (Fin m) (Fin k) R)
        ((MvPolynomial.universalFactorizationMap R n m k hn) (MvPolynomial.X j))) =
    if ↑j < ↑i then 0
    else if h : ↑j - ↑i < m then MvPolynomial.X (Sum.inl ⟨↑j - ↑i, h⟩) else if ↑j - ↑i = m then 1 else 0
items.informal_description: For variables $i$ and $j$, the partial derivative with respect to $\text{inr}(i)$ of the tensor product equivalence applied to the universal factorization map's variable $X_j$ is: $0$ if $j < i$; $X_{\text{inl}(j - i)}$ if $j - i < m$; $1$ if $j - i = m$; and $0$ otherwise. This describes how the partial derivative acts on the embedded variable in the tensor product structure of multivariate polynomial rings.

items.informal_name: Partial Derivative of Tensor Product Polynomial in Universal Factorization Context
items.type:
∀ (R : Type u_1) [inst : CommRing R] (n m k : ℕ) (hn : n = m + k) (i : Fin m) (j : Fin n),
  (MvPolynomial.pderiv (Sum.inl i))
      ((MvPolynomial.tensorEquivSum R (Fin m) (Fin k) R)
        ((MvPolynomial.universalFactorizationMap R n m k hn) (MvPolynomial.X j))) =
    if ↑j < ↑i then 0
    else if h : ↑j - ↑i < k then MvPolynomial.X (Sum.inr ⟨↑j - ↑i, h⟩) else if ↑j - ↑i = k then 1 else 0
items.informal_description: The partial derivative of the tensor-equivalent polynomial $ \text{tensorEquivSum}(R, \text{Fin} \, m, \text{Fin} \, k, R, \text{universalFactorizationMap}(R, n, m, k, h_n, X_j)) $ with respect to the variable $ \text{Sum.inl} \, i $ yields: $ 0 $ if $ j < i $; $ X_{\text{inr}(j - i)} $ if $ j - i < k $; $ 1 $ if $ j - i = k $; and $ 0 $ otherwise. This describes how differentiation interacts with tensor product structures in multivariate polynomial rings under universal factorization maps.

items.informal_name: Differential Basis Application in Submersive Presentation
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {S : Type v} {ι : Type w} {σ : Type t} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : CommRing S] [inst_2 : Algebra R S]
  [inst_3 : Finite σ] (P : Algebra.SubmersivePresentation R S ι σ) (i j : σ),
  P.basisDeriv i j = (MvPolynomial.aeval P.val) ((MvPolynomial.pderiv (P.map j)) (P.relation i))
items.informal_description: For a submersive presentation $ P $ of an $ R $-algebra $ S $ with finite generating set $ \sigma $, the basis element $ \text{basisDeriv}_P(i,j) $ is given by evaluating the algebra homomorphism $ \text{aeval}_{P.\text{val}} $ on the partial derivative of $ P.\text{map}(j) $ with respect to the relation $ P.\text{relation}(i) $. That is, $ \text{basisDeriv}_P(i,j) = \text{aeval}_{P.\text{val}}\left(\frac{\partial}{\partial x_i} P.\text{map}(j)\right) $, where $ x_i $ corresponds to the generator indexed by $ i $.

items.informal_name: Differential of Algebra Evaluation at Single Generator in Submersive Presentation
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {S : Type v} {ι : Type w} {σ : Type t} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : CommRing S] [inst_2 : Algebra R S]
  (P : Algebra.PreSubmersivePresentation R S ι σ) [inst_3 : Finite σ] [inst_4 : DecidableEq σ] (i j : σ),
  P.aevalDifferential (Pi.single i 1) j = (MvPolynomial.aeval P.val) ((MvPolynomial.pderiv (P.map j)) (P.relation i))
items.informal_description: For a pre-submersive presentation $ P $ of an $ R $-algebra $ S $, evaluating the differential map $ \text{aevalDifferential} $ at the function $ \Pi.\text{single}(i, 1) $ (which is 1 at index $ i $ and 0 elsewhere) applied to index $ j $ yields the evaluation of the partial derivative of the $ j $-th relation with respect to the $ i $-th generator. Formally, $ P.\text{aevalDifferential}(\delta_i)(j) = \text{aeval}_P(\partial_{x_i}(\text{relation}_j)) $, where $ \delta_i $ denotes the indicator function at $ i $.

items.informal_name: Differential of Algebra Evaluation in Submersive Presentation
items.type:
{R : Type u} →
  {S : Type v} →
    {ι : Type w} →
      {σ : Type t} →
        [inst : CommRing R] →
          [inst_1 : CommRing S] →
            [inst_2 : Algebra R S] → Algebra.PreSubmersivePresentation R S ι σ → [Finite σ] → (σ → S) →ₗ[S] σ → S
items.informal_description: The linear map on the function space $\sigma \to S$ defined by evaluating the partial derivatives of relations in the algebra presentation with respect to generators, using the algebra evaluation homomorphism. For each basis element $j \in \sigma$, it maps $i \in \sigma$ to the evaluation of the partial derivative of the $j$-th relation with respect to the $i$-th generator in the polynomial ring.
